text: Who was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress?
explanation: Annie Besant presided over the Calcutta session in 1917. Sarojini Naidu was the first 'Indian' woman president (1925).

text: Which article of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to appoint a Prime Minister?
explanation: Article 75(1) states that the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.

text: What is the name of the boundary line between India and China?
explanation: The McMahon Line was drawn during the Simla Accord of 1914. Radcliffe Line is between India and Pakistan.

text: In which city is the 'Silent Valley National Park' located?
explanation: Silent Valley is located in the Nilgiri Hills, Palakkad district of Kerala, and is famous for its biodiversity.

text: Who is the author of the famous book 'Discovery of India'?
explanation: Nehru wrote this book while imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort (1942–1946).

text: Which planet is known as the 'Morning Star' or 'Evening Star'?
explanation: Venus is the brightest natural object in Earth's night sky after the Moon.

text: Who was the founder of the Gupta Dynasty?
explanation: Sri Gupta founded the dynasty around 240 CE. Chandragupta I was the first powerful king of the dynasty.

text: Which river is known as the 'Dakshin Ganga' (Ganges of the South)?
explanation: Godavari is the largest peninsular river and is nicknamed Dakshin Ganga due to its size and length.

text: The 'Fundamental Rights' in the Indian Constitution are inspired by which country?
explanation: The Bill of Rights of the US Constitution influenced Part III of the Indian Constitution.

text: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
explanation: Mountbatten served until 1948. C. Rajagopalachari was the first and only 'Indian' Governor-General.

text: Which state of India shares boundaries with maximum number of other states?
explanation: Uttar Pradesh shares borders with 8 states and 1 Union Territory (Delhi).

text: The 'Panchayati Raj' system was first introduced in which state of India?
explanation: It was inaugurated by Nehru in Nagaur district, Rajasthan, on 2nd October 1959.

text: Which fuel is used in 'Gas Turbines' for thermal power plants?
explanation: Natural gas is the primary fuel for gas-powered electricity generation.

text: Who was the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest?
explanation: Bachendri Pal achieved this feat in 1984.

text: The 'Kaziranga National Park' is famous for which animal?
explanation: Kaziranga (Assam) hosts two-thirds of the world's great one-horned rhinoceroses.

text: Which chemical is known as 'Oil of Vitriol'?
explanation: H2SO4 is called Oil of Vitriol because it was historically obtained by distilling certain green sulfates (vitriols).

text: Who is known as the 'Shakespeare of India'?
explanation: Kalidasa was a Sanskrit writer and poet, famous for 'Abhigyan Shakuntalam'.

text: Which city is known as the 'Queen of the Arabian Sea'?
explanation: Kochi (Cochin) was a major trade hub for spices and an important port city for centuries.

text: The first session of the Indian National Congress (1885) was held in which city?
explanation: It was held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay, presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee.

text: What is the capital of 'Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu'?
explanation: After the merger in 2020, Daman was designated as the capital of the united Union Territory.

text: Which Vitamin is also known as 'Ascorbic Acid'?
explanation: Vitamin C (found in citrus fruits) is essential for repair of tissues and enzymatic production of certain neurotransmitters.

text: The 'Sun Temple' of Konark was built by which dynasty?
explanation: King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty built the temple in the 13th century.

text: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?
explanation: Ambedkar is known as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.

text: Which gas is filled in 'Electric Bulbs'?
explanation: Inert gases (Argon/Nitrogen) prevent the tungsten filament from oxidizing.

text: Which is the smallest planet in our solar system?
explanation: Mercury is the smallest planet. Pluto is classified as a 'dwarf planet'.

text: Who invented the 'Dynamics of Civilizations' theory of History?
explanation: Toynbee's 'A Study of History' explores the rise and fall of 26 civilizations.

text: What is the study of 'Coins' called?
explanation: Numismatics is the study or collection of currency, including coins, tokens, and bank notes.

text: Who is the first law officer of the Government of India?
explanation: Article 76 provides for the appointment of the Attorney General of India by the President.

text: In which state is the 'Hampi' ruins located?
explanation: Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

text: Who was the 'Rani of Jhansi's' birth name?
explanation: Manikarnika Tambe became Rani Lakshmibai after marrying Raja Gangadhar Rao of Jhansi.

text: The 'Gandhi-Irwin Pact' was signed in which year?
explanation: It was signed before the Second Round Table Conference, leading to the suspension of the Civil Disobedience Movement.

text: Which instrument is used to measure 'Atmospheric Pressure'?
explanation: A barometer measures the weight of the air above a given point.

text: Who was the first Indian to win a 'Nobel Prize'?
explanation: Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for 'Gitanjali'.

text: Which port of India is known as the 'Child of Partition'?
explanation: Kandla (Gujarat) was developed after the Karachi port went to Pakistan following Partition.

text: Who is called the 'Nightingale of India'?
explanation: Mahatma Gandhi gave her this title because of the lyrical quality of her poetry.

text: The 'Khajuraho' temples were built by which dynasty?
explanation: The temples in Madhya Pradesh were built between 950 and 1050 CE by the Chandelas.

text: On which river is the 'Sardar Sarovar Dam' built?
explanation: The dam in Gujarat is one of the largest concrete gravity dams in the world.

text: What is the full form of 'NITI' in NITI Aayog?
explanation: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.

text: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the 'Directive Principles of State Policy' (DPSP)?
explanation: Articles 36 to 51 cover DPSP, aiming to create a welfare state.

text: What is the currency of 'Japan'?
explanation: JPY (Yen) is a major global currency.

text: Which of these is NOT a fundamental right in India?
explanation: Right to Property was removed from Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment (1978) and made a legal right.

text: Who founded the 'Aarya Samaj'?
explanation: Founded in 1875 in Bombay, its motto was 'Back to the Vedas'.

text: The 'Mountbatten Plan' of June 3, 1947, was related to?
explanation: The plan proposed the partition of India into two independent dominions.

text: Which planet is the largest in the solar system?
explanation: Jupiter is a gas giant and has a mass 2.5 times that of all the other planets combined.

text: What is the capital of 'Israel'?
explanation: While most countries maintain embassies in Tel Aviv, Israel claims Jerusalem as its capital.

text: Under which article of the Indian Constitution 'Untouchability' is abolished?
explanation: Article 17 is a significant civil rights provision in the Constitution.

text: The 'Rowlatt Act' was passed in which year?
explanation: The act was called 'Black Act' and led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

text: Who was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic Silver medal?
explanation: Sindhu won silver in Badminton at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

text: On which island is 'Port Blair' located?
explanation: Port Blair is the capital of Andaman and Nicobar Islands and is situated on South Andaman.

text: Who is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'?
explanation: Naoroji was the first Indian to be a British MP and a founder of the INC.
